preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for x in stdin.split()[:1])
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of planks.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in stdin.split()[1:1+n])
preconditions.description: The second line contains n space-separated integers h1, h2, ..., hn (1 ≤ hi ≤ 10^9) representing the heights of the planks.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for x in stdin.split()[1+n:1+n+1])
preconditions.description: The third line is a single integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 10^5) representing the number of queries.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdin.split()[1+n+1:1+n+1+2*q:2]) and all(int(x) >= int(y) for x, y in zip(stdin.split()[1+n+1:1+n+1+2*q:2], stdin.split()[1+n+2:1+n+1+2*q:2]))
preconditions.description: Each query consists of two integers li and ri (1 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ n) representing the boundaries of a piece of the fence.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.split()) == q) and all(stdout.split()[i].isdigit() for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly q integers, one per query, representing the number of distinct matching pieces for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout.split()[i]) <= n for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a non-negative count of matching pieces, bounded by the total number of planks n.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda: (h := [int(x) for x in stdin.split()[1:1+n]]), (queries := [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in zip(stdin.split()[1+n+1:1+n+1+2*q:2], stdin.split()[1+n+2:1+n+1+2*q:2])]), (outputs := [int(x) for x in stdout.split()]), all((lambda l, r: (width := r - l + 1), (target := h[l-1:r]), (sum_target := sum(target)), (avg_target := sum_target / width), (all(h[l-1+i] == avg_target for i in range(width))), (all((lambda l2, r2: (width2 := r2 - l2 + 1), (width == width2), (l2 < l or r2 > r), (all(h[l2-1+i] == avg_target - h[l+i] for i in range(width))))(l2, r2) for l2 in range(1, n+1) for r2 in range(l2, n+1) if (l2 < l or r2 > r) and (r2 - l2 + 1 == width)) == outputs[i]))(queries[i][0], queries[i][1]) for i in range(q))
postconditions.description:
For each query (li, ri), the output is the count of distinct pieces (l2, r2) such that:
1. The piece (l2, r2) does not intersect with (li, ri).
2. The piece (l2, r2) has the same width as (li, ri).
3. For all i (0 ≤ i ≤ width-1), the sum of heights at positions li+i and l2+i equals the sum of heights at positions li and l2 (i.e., hl1+i + hl2+i = hl1 + hl2).
This is equivalent to the heights of the piece (l2, r2) being the reflection of the heights of (li, ri) around the average height of (li, ri).
